jobs.name: night-glass
jobs.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: one finished portrait-format photographic Overprint artwork for the music film IN THE CITY by Caveman, filmmaker Philip Di Fiore. Generate only the art, absolutely no text or lettering.
EDIT TARGET: Image 1, the original pale photograph of the woman with the existing faint mirror reflection to her left. Preserve this actual woman's identity, exact facial structure, eye shape and gaze, open-lipped expression, hair, head angle, pose and the source photograph's left-side reflection. Her substantial, tonal photographic face must dominate. This is a treatment of THIS photograph, not a substitute portrait. Restore subtle photographic definition naturally without changing facial features.
STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: Image 2, the existing blue/orange Overprint artwork. Take its tactile analog printed-collage quality, photographic grain, fine halftone, paper/ink wear and tiny registration artifacts. Do not copy its blue/orange palette or rectangular grid. Keep nuanced skin tones and a rich photographic tonal range; no posterized flat vector face, overexposed white face, waxy synthetic skin, or plastic digital filter.
Composition: portrait 4:5, approximately 1122 by 1402 pixels; edge-to-edge artwork with no border or letterbox. Retain the main face and both actual eyes clearly, plus the original spectral reflection on the left. Leave the lower-right neck/clothing region relatively quiet and dark enough for a small HTML title cutout added later; do not draw a title card, box or placeholder.
Hard constraints: no text, UI, typography, logos, watermarks, buildings, city skyline, new objects, new people, inset pictures, picture-in-picture, or invented extra duplicated faces. Only the mirror reflection already present in Image 1 may remain.
Direction: NIGHT GLASS. Make a sophisticated, unsettling, nocturnal analog cinematic print, using the source reflection as an offset vertical spectral band viewed through smoked glass. Rich petrol and cyan inks, obsidian shadows and luminous mercury-silver highlights, with only a few sodium-amber flashes. Skin retains gentle warm undertones and real dark-to-light modeling; silver should read like metallic photographic light, never blank white.
Composition and material: inventive irregular translucent ink planes and fractured narrow strips at asymmetrical angles frame the face without covering or cutting through the eyes. The ghost band at the left is the original mirror image only, soft, partially veiled and integrated with the smoked-glass texture; not a second inset portrait. A few fine scuffs, subtle scratches and misregistered ink contours create real printed depth. Dark petrol occupies the perimeter and bottom-right, while the main face has ample luminous, nuanced photographic substance. Create moody nocturnal city feeling entirely through reflected light and ink; do not add city objects. A beautiful, tense physical art print, distinct from the reference's orthogonal blue/orange grid.
